title: Error Recovery
concept: Error recovery allows the compiler to continue after encountering errors — reporting multiple issues in one compilation instead of stopping at the first error.
why: Stopping at the first error wastes time. Error recovery reports all issues at once, enabling faster fix cycles and better IDE integration.
tips: Error recovery enables 'fix all at once' workflows — read all errors before fixing any
The first error is usually real — subsequent errors may be cascaded from recovery stubs
IDEs depend on error recovery — without it, completions would break on every keystroke
Good error recovery is the difference between a helpful compiler and a frustrating one
common_mistakes: Fixing errors one at a time — read all errors first, plan fixes, then fix at once
Assuming all reported errors are real — some are cascaded from recovery stubs (false positives)
Not configuring max-errors properly — 5 is enough for a first pass, increase if debugging
